description.value: Structural MRI morphometry study comparing regional brain volumes in children with and without prenatal cocaine exposure at 8–10 years, including dose-response analyses of maternal substance exposure levels.

spans.text: In order to explore whether cocaine exposure in utero leads to long-term alterations in volumetric brain growth, that may be evident globally, or restricted to particularly vulnerable structures, we performed structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of prenatally cocaine exposed (CE) and non-cocaine exposed (NCE) children.

value: We hypothesize that structural markers of altered brain development may yield valuable clinical markers for assessment, monitoring and treatment of prenatally drug-exposed offspring.
